changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: One system for the tills and the website. One customer, one basket, one vendor accountable, so you never have two vendors pointing at each other. Then show it: an online order returned at a store till, live. For retail buyers with stores, especially the store operations owner.
changes.why: The buyer's own words (one system, one customer, one basket, no vendors pointing at each other) are sharper than our 'line has disappeared' claim, which got silence and the reply 'that's a diagram.'

changes.change: Add a proof kit for retail deals with stores: a named rollout owner, a rollout plan template (dates, who installs, what happens to the old tills), and a bench of retail references with stores and online who can take a call within days. Use it in place of 'we'll bring in a partner'.
changes.why: The deal turned at the store ops workshop, where we had no store rollout experience, a partner answer, no rollout plan and no reference call in time.

changes.change: Open unified-commerce conversations with the failure the buyer lived through: 'Buy online, return in store, and the till can't see the order. Loyalty that doesn't work because store and web are two customer records.' Aim it at the COO or store operations owner, not only the ecommerce or technical lead.
changes.why: The trigger was store returns and a split customer record, and the COO who signed was met only once, so our web-led pitch spoke to the wrong person and the wrong pain.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For retail buyers with stores: replace 'see our customer stories' with 'talk to a retailer running tills and web on one system', and offer a live reference call, not a case study. Name retailers the buyer would know.
changes.why: The buyer asked 'can I talk to them?' and we sent no call in time, while Adyen named retailers the COO knew.
